analysis.title: GS Crypto: Monthly On-chain & Market Data (Sep 2026)
key_insights: BTC finished September at about $84K, +6.4% MoM. It opened near $79K, fell to $75K mid-month when the CLARITY Act stalled, then cleared the $82K ceiling that had rejected it throughout August.
BTC reached a new high of $87.3K mid-month, its best since January, absorbing both the CLARITY failure and the Fed raising its policy rate. It then faded into month end.
ETH and SOL finished September +8.9% and +14.6% MoM respectively, lifted by the BTC breakout.
US-listed spot ETFs took in net inflows of +$2.4bn (BTC), +$634mm (ETH) and +$262mm (SOL) in September. GS says this offset an increasingly challenging macro backdrop.
BTC broke through $86.5K in the first two sessions of October (Bloomberg). October has been BTC's strongest month, with a mean return of +15.4% (MarketView).
GS describes the macro setup as benign yet fragile. Growth is holding up and the Fed hike debate slipped to December. The dominant risks are energy, long-end yields and AI-complex debt issuance.
The CLARITY Act failed a Senate procedural vote on September 15, which GS calls the defining policy event of the month.

After the vote, the SEC issued a five-year 'Innovation Exemption' setting a pathway for trading tokenized equities on certain venues. It also proposed allowing investment advisers to hold certain client cryptocurrencies in custody, and gave further guidance on token buybacks and staking.

The CFTC issued a no-action letter easing introducing-broker registration for certain software providers. It also updated guidance on tokenized money-market funds as collateral and on using public and private blockchains for recordkeeping.
BTC trusted spot volume rose +14.4% MoM and CME front 3-month futures volume rose +5.7% MoM. Aggregate US-listed BTC spot ETF AUM is back above $100bn.
Bitcoin network activity was largely flat. Average daily value transferred rose +12.0% MoM. Miner revenues rose with price, and miner supply sent to exchanges fell -24.1% MoM.
ETH/BTC rose +2.4% MoM. ETH trusted spot volume rose +32.2% and CME front 3-month futures volume rose +32.1% MoM. US-listed ETH spot ETF AUM is $16.3bn.

Ethereum average daily transaction count fell -16.1% MoM and new addresses fell -13.8%. Average daily value transferred rose +447.8% MoM. Layer 2 blob-carrying transactions rose +13.1% and blob fees rose +88.9% MoM. Monthly total ETH burnt rose +60.6%.
SOL/BTC rose +7.7% and SOL/ETH rose +5.2% MoM. SOL trusted spot volume rose +25.0% and CME front 3-month futures volume rose +40.2% MoM. US-listed SOL spot ETF AUM totals $1.8bn across 6 ETFs.

Solana network activity was broadly positive. Average daily active addresses rose +37.4%, transaction count +11.7% and value transferred +16.5% MoM. Validator revenue rose +13.1%, delegator revenue +16.5% and monthly SOL burnt +7.8% MoM.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BTC absorbed the rate raise and still reached a new high of $87.3K. GS says the debate over a further Fed hike slipped to December.

crypto_views: BTC ended September +6.4% MoM at about $84K, with a high of $87.3K, its best since January.
BTC cleared the $82K ceiling that had rejected it throughout August. It broke $86.5K in the first two sessions of October (Bloomberg).
October has been BTC's strongest month, with a mean return of +15.4% (MarketView). GS says all eyes are on whether BTC can extend its climb.
Spot ETF inflows in September were +$2.4bn (BTC), +$634mm (ETH) and +$262mm (SOL). BTC ETF AUM is above $100bn, ETH ETF AUM is $16.3bn and SOL ETF AUM is $1.8bn.

The CLARITY Act failed a Senate procedural vote on September 15. The SEC and CFTC then moved to fill the gap with an Innovation Exemption for tokenized equities, a custody proposal for investment advisers, staking and buyback guidance, and CFTC collateral and recordkeeping guidance.
ETH rose +8.9% MoM and ETH/BTC rose +2.4%. ETH burn rose +60.6% and Layer 2 blob fees rose +88.9% MoM.
SOL rose +14.6% MoM with SOL/BTC up +7.7%. Active addresses rose +37.4% and CME futures volume rose +40.2% MoM.
risk_factors: Energy prices, long-end yields and AI-complex debt issuance remain the dominant macro risks.
The Fed hike debate has slipped to December rather than being resolved.
The CLARITY Act failed its Senate procedural vote, so regulatory clarity is left to agency action.
Price across BTC, ETH and SOL faded into month end.
vol_and_positioning: CME front 3-month futures volumes rose +5.7% (BTC), +32.1% (ETH) and +40.2% (SOL) MoM.
Trusted spot volumes rose +14.4% (BTC), +32.2% (ETH) and +25.0% (SOL) MoM.
GS says price across the three majors faded into month end despite the ETF inflows, because of the challenging macro backdrop.

tension_points.bull_case: BTC has already broken $86.5K in the first two sessions of October. October is historically its strongest month at a mean return of +15.4% (MarketView). September ETF inflows were strong, with BTC at +$2.4bn.
tension_points.bear_case: The macro setup is benign yet fragile. Energy, long-end yields and AI-complex debt issuance remain in play, and the Fed hike debate has only slipped to December. Prices faded into month end despite the ETF inflows.

theme_stances.key_argument: BTC finished Q3 on a strong note and has already broken $86.5K in October, with seasonality supportive.
theme_stances.evidence: historical seasonality is supportive, with October being BTC's strongest month

theme_stances.key_argument: After the CLARITY Act failed its Senate vote, the SEC and CFTC issued exemptions, proposals and guidance that fill the regulatory vacuum.
